mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% in the month prior to decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of FEDFUNDS > 4.0% months, or the IC is positive with p < 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points coinciding with a monthly increase in GDPC1 signals labor market softening and consumer demand weakness, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: IC for the interaction is negative with p < 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in HOUST of at least 3% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating industrial demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-on-month > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in 80% of such HOUST expansion episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO below 90 (index 2017=100) followed by a rebound above 95 signals supply-side stress releasing, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 90 then INDPRO > 95 within the same month
failure_condition: IC remains negative (p > 0.05) or 20-day returns are negative in >50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for two consecutive months in a period of rising CPIAUCSL, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns as lower rates offset inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for 2 months and CPIAUCSL month-on-month > 0.2% in the same months
failure_condition: IC for the interaction is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or 20-day returns are not positive in >60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in PAYEMS below 130,000 followed by a sustained rise above 135,000 suggests improving labor market absorption, predicting positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 130,000 then PAYEMS > 135,000 within the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >40% of such episodes, or IC is negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both RSAFS and GDPC1 exceeding 2% each indicate dual demand pressures, forecasting negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as over-supplied markets react.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-on-month > 2% AND GDPC1 month-on-month > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: IC for the interaction is positive (p < 0.05) or 20-day returns are not negative in >70% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A regime of falling UNRATE (< 5%) combined with a sustained rise in HOUST (> 4%) over a 3-month window predicts positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as soft labor offsets weak supply.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for 3 months and HOUST month-on-month > 4% over the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in 75% of such episodes, or interaction IC is not significant (p > 0.05).
